column1: # verbs.tsv (harbor#1428) — the task verbs a repo's justfile answers, and which kinds of repo must carry each.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `just test` meant a different thing in every repo, and a scaffolded repo got a verb set
# that its own scaffolder and its controller did not carry (harbor#1428, measured 2026-11-01). One row per verb
# says what it means and what its exit code promises, so the same word means the same thing everywhere; the
# `kinds` cell says which repo-kinds.tsv kinds must have it. `bin/lint-name.sh --check repo-kind <dir>` reads the
# recipe names of <dir>/justfile and reports a required verb it lacks as name.repo-verb; the fleet audit calls it.

# yard renders the verb set of a scaffolded repo's justfile from this file (tools/generate_justfile.py there; a stack's own recipes stay in tools/justfile-recipes/, and a required verb a stack lacks renders as a stub that exits non-zero).
# An exemption is a row in the repo's own naming-exemptions.tsv: rule name.repo-verb, subject repo-verb:<id>.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> meaning <TAB> exit <TAB> kinds <TAB> note
#   id      the recipe name, a bare lowercase kebab word
#   meaning what running it does, one clause
#   exit    what the exit code promises: always 0 = done, non-zero = the thing is not so; a verb that cannot run
#           here says so and exits non-zero (never a silent 0)
#   kinds   space-separated repo-kinds.tsv ids that must carry the verb; - when no kind must (an optional verb
#           the standard still names, so its meaning is the same where it exists)
#   note    why the kinds are the ones they are
